Position Summary

The Hospice Social Worker is responsible for modeling the Compassus values of Compassion, Integrity, Excellence, Teamwork, and Innovation and for promoting the Compassus philosophy, using the 6 Pillars of Success as the foundation. S/he is responsible for upholding the Code of Ethical Conduct and for promoting positive working relationships within the company, among all departments, and all external stakeholders. The Hospice Social Worker provides preventive, educational, and evaluative and treatment services to meet the psychosocial needs of patients and their families, to help them improve, restore, and maintain their maximum level of coping. S/he utilizes community resources and the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to aid in this process.

Position Specific Responsibilities

Explains hospice services and Medicare benefits to patients and families; obtains Informed Consent and Election of Benefits documents as requested.
Submits appropriate documentation and paperwork to facilities at the completion of patient visits; documentation is completed and submitted timely according to company policy.
Participates as a member of the IDT, including development and implementation of the plan of care.
Provides psycho-social support and counseling services to the patient and family; supports the involvement of external counseling resources commensurate with patient/family needs and scope of practice.
Assists in identifying the need for intervention of other IDT members.
Effectively communicates patient and family needs to IDT.
Collaborates with IDT to coordinate psycho-social care and support for the patient and family to ensure appropriateness, continuity, and quality of care.
Maintains updated, comprehensive care plans which reflect current problems, goals and interventions for patients.
Maintains respect for the family's environment and belief systems, and remains nondiscriminatory regarding age, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, physical or mental disability, and other personal matters.
Completes initial and ongoing psycho-social assessments for patients; identifies and addresses concerns/issues related to financial means, insurance, living arrangements/placement for long-term care, caregiver stressors, pre-bereavement and anticipatory grief, and community resource needs.
Facilitates placement in long-term care as warranted and monitors adjustment.
Participates in care planning meetings at long-term care facilities.
Supports and facilitates advance planning including living will/POA documents, funeral arrangements, memorial services, and body/organ donation.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from leaders, team members, investors, and external parties. Strong written and verbal communications.
Other Skills and Abilities: Ability to understand, read, write, and speak English. Articulates and embraces hospice philosophy.

SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)
is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

La mission

In response to the attacks of 7 October 2023, the Israeli army launched a massive offensive in the Gaza Strip, beginning with a campaign of air strikes followed by a series of ground offensives that successively hit all the enclave's governorates. The intensity of the fighting, repeated strikes and successive evacuation orders have forced more than 1.7 million people to move, sometimes several times, to sites less directly affected by the fighting. The first displacements towards the south of Gaza, and more particularly the governorate of Rafah where 1.7 million Palestinians were displaced in April 2024, were followed by the displacement of more than 1 million people towards the central part of the Gaza Strip when the offensive on Rafah was launched in May 2024.

Displaced people are living in schools, organised sites and informal sites where it is more difficult to organise assistance. The destruction by the fighting of vital infrastructure, such as health facilities, water and electricity supplies, schools and other public services, is having a major impact on the displaced and host populations.

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONA
L teams have been working in Gaza since February 2024. Activities are currently being developed in the governorate of Deir el-Balah, in the centre of the Gaza Strip, where a base was opened in March.

SI teams are implementing WASH activities, which include the installation and rehabilitation of water desalination plants to ensure the production of drinking water, the transport of water to displacement sites by tanker truck, and activities aimed at reducing health risks and improving the living conditions of displaced people through hygiene promotion sessions and the distribution of hygiene kits.

About The Position

Please Note: Review of applications will begin on September 25, 2026.

Under the supervision of the AVP/Dean of Students and work lead direction of the Wellness Services Coordinator the Health Educator engages the campus community in evidence-based approaches to support student wellness and disseminate data to drive findings of associated programs. This position will coordinate operations for the WellNest including food pantry appointments, operational procedures for food storage, food distribution, providing health resources, and cooking demonstrations.

The Health Educator regularly collaborates with university committees to implement strategic initiatives to address the wellbeing needs of students. This position is responsible to assess, design, implement, and evaluate wellbeing programs. Additionally, the Health Educator regularly conducts workshops and outreach events promoting campus resources, as well as implements wellbeing messaging through social marketing approaches. The Health Educator inform wellbeing issues pertinent to a university setting including but not limited to Basic Needs - food & housing security, Alcohol, Tobacco, & Other Drugs (ATOD), Cold/Flu, Nutrition/Fitness, Self-Care, Sexual Health, and Violence Prevention. This position provides guidance for wellbeing campaigns, programs and services offered within the WellNest and Wellness Center. The Health Educator also works closely with campus partners to support promotion of wellness services and leadership development for student assistants.

The position works closely with Peer Advocates for Wellness (PAW) student assistants for scheduling office hours and monitoring weekly assignments. The Health Educator develops projects, outreach events, learning outcomes, professional development, and training. The Health Educator will also coordinate and mentor PAW students in providing services in a client-centered, trauma informed approach.

The Health Educator collaborates with the Director and Wellbeing Services Coordinator to inform needs for departmental purchases, office and outreach supplies. The Health Educator must be able to lift up to 20 pounds and will occasionally require work in the evenings and weekends for outreach events/workshops and presentations.

Responsibilities

Department Support and Daily Operations

Coordinate daily WellNest operations in support of health education, wellness promotion, and student access to basic needs resources, including coordinating food pantry appointments, connecting students with appropriate health and wellness resources, providing informational tours, greeting and assisting visitors, supporting food demonstrations, and addressing other operational needs that facilitate delivery of health education and wellness services.
Facilitate and maintain best-practice procedures for food storage, distribution, and sanitation to support nutrition, food safety, and food security programming, ensuring adherence to county and state safe-food handling guidelines and adapting practices based on the changing health and wellness needs of the student population.
Coordinate food procurement and food access efforts in support of student nutrition, food security, and wellness initiatives through partnerships with Pioneer Dining, food recovery programs, the Alameda County Community Food Bank, food drives, and other campus and community resources.
Maintain operational records, utilization data, program logs, and reporting procedures for WellNest services to assess student participation and needs, evaluate service delivery, identify trends, and inform health education, wellness, and food security programming.
Support daily operations of the RAW Wellness Center to facilitate student access to health and wellness resources and programs, including coordinating relaxation room and Wii appointments, providing informational tours, greeting and assisting visitors, and connecting students with available wellness services and resources.

Wellbeing Educational and Consultative Functions

Assess, implement, and evaluate student needs on a variety of wellness topics including but not limited to basic needs, ATOD, nutrition, sexual health, stress management, and other topic areas pertinent to a college student population.
Maintain records and outcome data to prepare written and verbal reports. Support process/policy development for maintenance of accreditation documents.
Serve as departmental point of contact for food access and food security initiatives including but not limited to CalFresh/EBT sales initiatives, PAW Approved, initiatives with Pioneer Dining.
Participate in outreach, workshops, guest lectures, housing events, and other presentations that represent campaigns, programs, and services provided by RWUU.

Student Leadership Development

Facilitate didactic training, practicum experience, and student leader meetings.
Develop projects and outreach assignments that align with learning outcomes. 
Provide training and skill development for implementation of the wellbeing topics. 
Ensure staffing levels are scheduled for service delivery within the WellNest and to implement outreach activities and events.
Support mentorship, leadership development, professional growth, and career readiness of department student assistants. 

Administration and Collaboration

Collaborates with campus partners within the Division of Student Affairs and academic units to develop and implement programs and events that contribute to student success.
Collaborate with the Director and department staff to develop annual budget projections for operational, programming and outreach needs.
Collaborate with the Directors of Student Health & Counseling Services to identify and employ opportunities for clinical collaboration, appropriate healthcare practices, and facility usage that support student access to services.
Maintain relationships with external partners, vendors, community-based organizations to enhance program offerings and secure additional resources.

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience

SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)
is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

La mission

In response to the attacks of 7 October 2023, the Israeli army launched a massive offensive in the Gaza Strip, beginning with a campaign of air strikes followed by a series of ground offensives that successively hit all the enclave's governorates. The intensity of the fighting, repeated strikes and successive evacuation orders have forced more than 1.7 million people to move, sometimes several times, to sites less directly affected by the fighting. The first displacements towards the south of Gaza, and more particularly the governorate of Rafah where 1.7 million Palestinians were displaced in April 2024, were followed by the displacement of more than 1 million people towards the central part of the Gaza Strip when the offensive on Rafah was launched in May 2024.

Displaced people are living in schools, organised sites and informal sites where it is more difficult to organise assistance. The destruction by the fighting of vital infrastructure, such as health facilities, water and electricity supplies, schools and other public services, is having a major impact on the displaced and host populations.

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONA
L teams have been working in Gaza since February 2024. Activities are currently being developed in the governorate of Deir el-Balah, in the centre of the Gaza Strip, where a base was opened in March.

SI teams are implementing WASH activities, which include the installation and rehabilitation of water desalination plants to ensure the production of drinking water, the transport of water to displacement sites by tanker truck, and activities aimed at reducing health risks and improving the living conditions of displaced people through hygiene promotion sessions and the distribution of hygiene kits.

The Health Educator develops projects, outreach events, learning outcomes, professional development, and training.
